whatItIs.statement: A composable, themeable, and customizable sidebar.

whenNotToUse.statement: Do not implement navigation with a button-backed SidebarMenuButton whose onClick assigns the location or calls a navigation function. A navigation item must be a native link so it keeps its href, link role, Enter activation, modified-click and open-in-new-tab behaviour.

howToUse.statement: For a sidebar item that navigates to another page or view (a navigation item), compose SidebarMenuButton with a native anchor through asChild: Follow-ups. The anchor is the menu button itself, so do not nest a Button or a second link inside it. Its href is the destination and its text content is the accessible name; Enter activation, modified click, middle click, and open in new tab remain native browser behaviour.

To show which navigation item is the current page, set isActive on that SidebarMenuButton for the visual state and put aria-current="page" on the authored anchor: Follow-ups. isActive only sets the data-active styling and never adds aria-current, so the anchor owns current-page semantics. Mark exactly the one link for the page being shown, and never put aria-current on an action button. If a router link component sets aria-current itself, such as a NavLink, let the router own it rather than authoring it twice.

For a sidebar item that performs an action instead of navigating, such as expanding a section, opening an account menu, or running a command, use SidebarMenuButton without asChild: it renders a native button. Do not turn action items into anchors and do not give them href or aria-current. Navigation items are anchors; action items are buttons.

SidebarMenuButton does not own application routing and performs no client-side navigation. A plain anchor with href navigates natively. A framework router link component can be passed as the asChild child when it renders an anchor and forwards its props and ref, and the router then owns navigation.

The disabled attribute applies to button items only. On an anchor, aria-disabled only adds inert, dimmed styling (pointer-events-none and reduced opacity); it does not stop keyboard activation of an anchor that has an href. The design system adds no disabled-link behaviour and intercepts no link activation, so for a destination that is unavailable do not render the link, or render a non-navigating placeholder instead of an anchor with href.

In the icon-collapsed presentation, an anchor menu button keeps its link role, href, aria-current, keyboard focus, and accessible name from its content, so keep the label text inside the anchor. The tooltip prop adds a tooltip for the collapsed item without changing that name, and requires a TooltipProvider ancestor.

options.statement: Use the collapsible icon mode when the sidebar should collapse to icons.
